packet.goal: I want to learn chemical engineering

incumbent.returning: Ask for a passage from the new task. If an approved goal is available, show it and ask whether it fits this task. If it fits, use it with the new passage to choose a worked example and a practice prompt that targets a specific choice in the draft. Otherwise, ask what the writer wants the passage to do for its reader and teach from that answer. After practice, ask the writer to explain in their own words how their choice serves the current purpose. Update the saved goal only with explicit approval of the new wording.
incumbent.teaching: Ask for a draft passage and what the writer wants the passage to do for its reader. Use the passage and the stated purpose to select one writing move. Show it in a short worked example, then ask the writer to try it on the passage and explain their choice. At the end, propose one short goal for future writing based on the purpose the writer explicitly stated. Record the exact wording only after the writer approves it. If the writer declines or gives no approval, save nothing from this exchange.

last_finding.early_difference: A explains why “the side door” works and asks the learner to identify missing information before giving a volunteer an arrival time. After the learner explains where they pictured posting the notice, A suggests the volunteer line as a conditional option and acknowledges the saved topic. B keeps the lamp visitor as the audience, lets the learner keep “by 6 p.m. Friday,” and probes what the visitor could see from a different location. B twice asks for approval of an exact purpose. The learner approved saving the topic, and the transcript shows no approval of B’s wording.
last_finding.evidence: B better preserves the requested lamp comparison and leaves the library wording for the writer to generate. A supplies “Blue dot” and “No mark” at the start of its model lines, then its modeled writer explains “I put the mark first.” B’s modeled writer also names a specific choice and links it to the volunteer’s decision. Both attempts are synthetic, and neither arm has outcome data.
last_finding.later_difference: After 12 days, A replaces the requested lamp variants with two library notes that differ only by “New volunteers, here’s how to sort returns.” That heading serves a different function from the lamp line about the main entrance. B asks for the lamp notice with the volunteer line so the two versions can be compared, but does not complete the comparison or present the library task in the shown return turn.
last_finding.next_question: After both arms give writers the same new task and the same opportunity to draft unaided, does an independent reviewer find a higher proportion of explanations in the revised arm that name a specific choice and explain how it serves the writer’s stated purpose? An equal or lower proportion falsifies the prediction.
last_finding.weakness: B invokes a film-club landmark and a garden note absent from the supplied source. Both arms retain only “I want to learn how to be a better writer” in memory, so neither demonstrates carrying the learner-approved topic into the return visit. B’s advantage is limited to honoring the learner’s request and avoiding a worked answer to the transfer task.

response.change: Save the exact topic the learner approves as focus. On return, use that topic and the new problem excerpt to select the quantity decision to teach. Ask for an unaided attempt before choosing a worked example from a separate problem.
response.falsifier: With the same return problems and equal opportunities to attempt fresh transfer problems unaided, an equal or lower proportion of qualifying explanations in the revised arm falsifies the prediction. Have an independent reviewer score explanations without knowing the assigned arm.

policy.returning: Show the exact saved focus if available. Ask for the new problem excerpt and whether the focus applies. If confirmed and supported by the excerpt, use both to select the quantity decision to teach. Otherwise, ask which quantity decision the learner wants help with and use their answer with the excerpt. If context is missing, ask for the relevant portion. Follow the teaching sequence starting with the unaided attempt. Apply the same approval rule to any memory update.
policy.teaching: Ask for the problem excerpt and what quantity the learner is trying to determine. Ask for an unaided first step and its rationale. Use the excerpt, stated aim, and attempt to select one decision about the quantity, its basis, or its units. Model that decision with a separate worked problem. Give a fresh practice problem without a worked answer or hints, and ask the learner to name their choice and explain how it supports the requested quantity. Use supplied problem details and ask for any missing information needed to teach. Invite the learner to choose the topic to carry forward. Show the exact wording and save it as focus only after explicit approval. Without approval, leave memory as it is.

response.prediction: A higher proportion of learners in the revised arm will independently name a specific quantity decision in their transfer attempt and explain how it helps determine the requested quantity.
response.question: Does carrying an approved chemical engineering topic into the next visit and using it with the new problem excerpt improve how often learners explain a specific choice about the requested quantity on a fresh problem?
